title: The Clever Octopus
passage:
Octopuses have no bones, three hearts and blue blood, but their most remarkable feature may be their intelligence. Scientists think they are among the smartest invertebrates, which are animals without a backbone.

An octopus has roughly five hundred million nerve cells, a number similar to that of a dog. Surprisingly, about two thirds of these cells are located not in its brain but in its eight arms. As a result, each arm can taste, touch and react somewhat independently, almost as though it had a small mind of its own.

Researchers have observed octopuses solving complicated problems in laboratories. Some have learned to unscrew the lids of jars to reach food inside, and others have escaped from their tanks by squeezing through tiny openings. In the ocean, certain octopuses collect coconut shells and carry them across the seabed, later using them as portable shelters when danger approaches.

Octopuses are also masters of disguise. Special cells in their skin allow them to change color and texture within a fraction of a second, so they can blend into rocks, sand or coral almost perfectly.

Despite these abilities, most octopuses live only one or two years, and they do not learn from parents, because they hatch alone. Scientists remain fascinated by how such short-lived creatures develop such remarkable skills, and they continue to investigate how an animal so different from humans can think so cleverly.

questions.stem: Which word from the passage is an ADJECTIVE?
options: portable
shelters
escaped
almost
questions.why: 'Portable' describes the shelters, so it is an adjective.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the word 'disguise' correctly?
options: The octopus disguise quickly across the sand.
She ate a disguise for breakfast today.
The octopus used color as a disguise.
The disguise water was cold and deep.
questions.why: A disguise is something that hides who or what you are; only this sentence uses it correctly.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why can each octopus arm react somewhat on its own?
options: Each arm has its own separate heart
Its arms have no skin cells at all
Its brain is larger than a dog's
Most of its nerve cells are in its arms
questions.why: About two thirds of its nerve cells are located in its arms, 'as a result' each arm reacts independently.

questions.stem: Which idea does the writer present right AFTER describing the octopus's nerve cells?
options: Octopuses changing color and texture
Octopuses solving problems in labs
Octopuses having three hearts
Octopuses living one or two years
questions.why: Paragraph 3, about laboratory problem-solving, follows the paragraph on nerve cells.

questions.stem: In what way is an octopus SIMILAR to a dog?
options: Both have three hearts and blue blood
Both learn their skills from parents
Both live only one or two years
They have a similar number of nerve cells
questions.why: The passage says an octopus has about 500 million nerve cells, 'similar to that of a dog.'

questions.stem: The writer calls octopuses 'masters of disguise.' What does this phrase suggest?
options: They are extremely skilled at hiding
They teach other animals to hide
They wear masks made of coconuts
They rule over other sea creatures
questions.why: A 'master' is an expert; the phrase stresses their skill at blending in.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST expresses the writer's viewpoint?
options: Octopuses are dangerous and best avoided
Octopuses are no smarter than jellyfish
Octopuses are amazing animals worth studying
Octopuses should be kept as pets at home
questions.why: Words like 'remarkable' and 'fascinated' show the writer's admiration and interest.

questions.stem: Which information is LEAST clear in the passage?
options: How many hearts an octopus has
How octopuses gain skills without parents
What octopuses do with coconut shells
How long most octopuses usually live
questions.why: The writer says scientists still do not know how they develop such skills.

options: An octopus grows a backbone to escape danger
An octopus lives fifty years and teaches its young
An octopus changes color only once in its life
An octopus squeezes out of a tank through a gap
questions.why: The passage says octopuses have escaped tanks through tiny openings.

questions.stem: Which is the BEST alternative title for the passage?
options: The Clever Mind of the Octopus
Coconuts of the Tropical Beach
How Dogs Learn New Tricks
The Fastest Fish in the Ocean
questions.why: The whole passage is about octopus intelligence.
